name: T-Intersection
spec: yellow diamond with a black T-shaped symbol
meaning: The road ends ahead at a T; you must turn left or right.

snippets.back: At an unlit intersection, yield to traffic approaching from the right and proceed only with extreme caution when safe.
Solid white lines mark crosswalks at intersections and sometimes between them, and with no controlling signal a driver must stop at any crosswalk occupied by pedestrians.
If your planned turn is after an intersection, wait until you have crossed that intersection before signaling so another driver does not mistake your intended turn.
At a T intersection, the driver on the street that ends must yield to vehicles on the cross street.

Skip U-turns at posted signs, on crossings, over dividers and twin double yellows, under two-hundred-foot sight, on one-ways, at fire stations and driveways, in business blocks except intersections and openings.
Pedestrians have the right-of-way at intersections and crosswalks even where no lines are painted.

When a sign or signal requires a stop, you must stop before reaching the stop line, yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk, and stay alert for pedestrians at intersections because not all crosswalks are marked.
Pedestrian priority at intersections does not depend on crosswalk paint being present.

evidence: [sec09-card-sec09-F22 | AZ p.35] At a T intersection, the driver on the street that ends must yield to vehicles on the cross street.
result.summary: AZ snippet confirms a T intersection is where a street ends and requires yielding to cross street, consistent with road ending and needing to turn; no snippet describes shape/color.
